articles.title: Earliest known compact quasar pair poses a black hole growth puzzle
articles.description: The oldest pair of compact quasars ever observed has been found only 900 million years after the Big Bang. Scientists say there is no theoretical explanation for how the pair of actively feeding black holes grew so massive at such an early time in the history of the universe. The pair of quasars has been given the Hawaiian nickname Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Astronomers discovered the oldest compact quasar pair ever observed, appearing just 900 million years after the Big Bang. This remarkable find challenges current understanding of how supermassive black holes grow so rapidly in the early universe.

articles.title: NASA reveals bold new plan to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028
articles.description: NASA has revealed an accelerated plan to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028, with SpaceX and Blue Origin developing competing lunar landers and a crucial orbital test scheduled for 2027. Faster rocket preparations, new lightweight spacesuits, and redesigned missions could help pave the way for a permanent lunar presence and future human exploration of Mars.
articles.summary: NASA announced an accelerated plan to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028 with SpaceX and Blue Origin partnerships. This bold initiative marks a major milestone in humanity's return to lunar exploration.

articles.title: SpaceX moves Starship Flight 15 booster to launch pad for 'squeeze test' ahead of epic double-catch attempt (photos)
articles.description: SpaceX has moved its Starship Super Heavy booster to the pad to prep for the next test flight of the megarocket, a historic mission scheduled to launch this Friday (Nov. 13).
articles.summary: SpaceX prepares Starship Super Heavy booster for Flight 15, positioning the megarocket for a historic double-catch landing attempt.

articles.description: Follow live updates as SpaceX attempts its Starship Flight 15 test flight with first double landings.
articles.summary: SpaceX attempts Starship Flight 15 with Super Heavy booster positioned for the first-ever double landing test of the megarocket system.

articles.summary: NASA opens applications for astronauts to live and work on the Moon, marking an exciting milestone in lunar exploration and human spaceflight.

articles.summary: SpaceX is preparing for Starship 15's launch on November 13, featuring an ambitious double booster capture maneuver with Elon Musk estimating success as probable. This mission represents a major milestone in rapid reusability technology development.

articles.title: SpaceX, Blue Origin Winners As NASA Awards $10 Bil In Moon Base Contracts
articles.description: NASA over the weekend announced a wave of mission awards and updates as part of its effort to develop a base on the Moon. The agency awarded more than $10 billion in contracts to SpaceX, Blue Origin, Lockheed Martin and more. SPCX and other space stocks surge…
articles.summary: NASA awards $10 billion in contracts to SpaceX and Blue Origin for developing a lunar base infrastructure. This historic investment accelerates humanity's return to the Moon and establishes a foundation for sustained lunar presence.

articles.title: NASA Invites Media, Public to Join Voyager 1 One-Light Day Activities
articles.description: Launched nearly 50 years ago in 1977, NASA’s Voyager 1 on Wednesday, Nov. 18 will have traveled one light-day from Earth, which is more than 16 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object, and any light from Earth would take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft. NASA will highlight […]
articles.summary: NASA celebrates Voyager 1's extraordinary achievement of traveling one light-day from Earth nearly 50 years after its 1977 launch. The public is invited to join commemorative activities honoring this landmark interstellar milestone.

articles.title: NASA Scientists Show How Gravitational Waves Can Reveal New Worlds
articles.description: The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory, now in development, will detect gravitational waves, the tiny ripples in space-time caused by orbiting masses. Now two studies led by NASA astrophysicists show in new detail how LISA could reveal a new and unique population of exoplanets — worlds beyond our solar system — throughout our galaxy.  […]
articles.summary: NASA scientists reveal how the upcoming LISA observatory will detect gravitational waves to discover new worlds beyond traditional detection methods. This breakthrough detection technology promises to revolutionize exoplanet discovery.

articles.title: Automated Assembly in Space is the Future and NOM4D is Showing the Way
articles.description: The ability to build large structures in space is maturing. The ISS, Mir, and Tiangong were built in space from pre-constructed modules, but a new program called NOM4D is taking space construction to the next level. It recently showed that a simple robot can create truss-like structures in space from premade components. Is the sky the limit for NOM4D?
articles.summary: Automated assembly technologies are maturing in space, with NOM4D demonstrating the future of large-scale construction beyond Earth. Building on lessons from the ISS, Mir, and Tiangong, this capability will enable ambitious space infrastructure.

articles.title: First Direct Measurement of Cosmic Hydrogen Could Change How We Map the Universe
articles.description: The MeerKLASS international collaboration achieves the first direct measurement of the large-scale clustering of cosmic hydrogen in the Universe.
articles.summary: The MeerKLASS collaboration achieves the first direct measurement of cosmic hydrogen clustering at large scales. This breakthrough discovery will transform our methods for mapping the universe's structure.

articles.title: How ripples in space-time can reveal new exoplanets
articles.description: The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory, now in development, will detect gravitational waves, the tiny ripples in space-time caused by orbiting masses. Now two studies led by NASA astrophysicists show in new detail how LISA could reveal a new and unique population of exoplanets—worlds beyond our solar system—throughout our galaxy.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The LISA space observatory under development will use gravitational wave detection to reveal new exoplanets in innovative ways. This breakthrough method promises to unlock hidden worlds throughout the cosmos.

articles.title: Earth's 'core carbon' may have come from the far reaches of the solar system
articles.description: A new study suggests that most of Earth's carbon originated in the outer solar system and didn't arrive here until the late stages of planetary development. The study, led by researchers at Yale and Columbia, is based upon an analysis of magma droplets called "melt inclusions" from historic volcano eruptions in Hawaii, including the Keanakākoʻi eruptions from 1500 to 1840 and the Kīlauea Iki eruption in 1959.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: A new study reveals that most of Earth's carbon originated in the outer solar system and arrived later through planetary migration. This discovery illuminates the solar system's dynamic early history and Earth's composition origins.

articles.title: Webb's controversial 'little red dots' may finally have an explanation
articles.description: Astronomers may have solved one of the biggest mysteries uncovered by NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), using sophisticated simulations to show that enigmatic objects known as "little red dots" (LRDs) are likely the birthplaces of the first supermassive black holes.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Astronomers may have solved the mystery of JWST's puzzling 'little red dots' through innovative analysis. This breakthrough helps explain unexpected populations of distant galaxies revealed by the James Webb Space Telescope.

articles.title: Gravitational waves hint at black holes born from failed supernovae
articles.description: When the most massive stars in the universe die, they often detonate in fiery supernovae, dramatically blasting most of their matter into space. The remaining stellar cores collapse into neutron stars and, sometimes, black holes. However, theories suggest that some massive stars might die without a bang, instead directly collapsing inward to become neutron stars or black holes.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Gravitational wave observations suggest black holes can form from massive stars that fail to produce supernovae. This discovery expands our understanding of how black holes originate in the universe.

articles.title: Caltech robot makes history by building a structure in space
articles.description: For the first time, a robot has autonomously built part of a structure in space, demonstrating a breakthrough that could fundamentally change space exploration. The technology could one day allow scientists to construct enormous telescopes, communications antennas, and solar power stations in orbit, far beyond the size limits of today's rockets.
articles.summary: A Caltech robot made history by autonomously building part of a structure in space for the first time. This breakthrough demonstrates transformative potential for robotic construction in space environments.

articles.title: Astronomers discover hidden alien planet in James Webb images
articles.description: A breakthrough in telescope imaging could reveal countless alien worlds that have been hiding in plain sight. Scientists developed a new technique that uses a digital twin of the James Webb Space Telescope to remove the overwhelming glare of stars, making faint exoplanets two to 15 times easier to detect than with conventional methods. The technology has already uncovered a previously hidden planet in existing telescope data and could reveal many more.
articles.summary: Advanced James Webb telescope imaging techniques reveal previously hidden exoplanets, potentially unlocking discovery of countless alien worlds. This breakthrough in detection methods promises a revolution in exoplanet astronomy.

articles.title: Mysterious gas leaks suggest Mars may still be volcanically alive
articles.description: Mysterious gas emissions and fresh volcanic fissures suggest that Mars may not be geologically dead after all, with hot magma potentially still active deep underground. The discovery could point to hidden pockets of warmth and chemical energy capable of supporting microbial life beneath the Red Planet’s surface.
articles.summary: Mars may retain geological activity, with mysterious gas emissions and fresh volcanic fissures suggesting the planet is not completely geologically dead.

articles.title: A mysterious 93-billion-mile cosmic structure may be the wreckage of colliding worlds
articles.description: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope has revealed surprising new details about a mysterious, 93-billion-mile-long cloud of dark, fluffy dust that may have formed when massive planetary bodies collided. The discovery challenges previous assumptions about the structure and offers new clues about the violent birth of planetary systems.
articles.summary: Hubble Space Telescope reveals a 93-billion-mile cosmic structure that may be the remnants of colliding worlds, offering new insights into planetary formation.

articles.title: A distant exoplanet mysteriously vanished from sight. Astronomers just discovered why
articles.description: Astronomers have solved the mystery of an exoplanet that "disappeared" after seven years of observations.
articles.summary: Astronomers solve the mystery of a distant exoplanet that appeared to vanish after seven years of observations.

articles.title: Uranus has a weird magnetic field that's stumped scientists for 40 years — we may finally know why
articles.description: The lopsided magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune could be the product of extreme conditions inside the planets, increasing the electrical conductivity that enhances the dynamo effect.
articles.summary: Scientists may have finally solved the 40-year mystery of Uranus's unusual magnetic field through new understanding of extreme planetary conditions.

articles.title: Physicists step closer to the 'Zeptoverse' after 42-year particle search
articles.description: Physicists have found evidence of a particle decay so rare that it is expected to occur only around once in every 10 billion "beauty" particles. The result, from the upgraded LHCb experiment at CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC), follows a search spanning mor…
articles.summary: Physicists achieve a major breakthrough after 42 years, finding evidence of an extremely rare particle decay predicted to occur only once in 10 billion events.

articles.title: The Vera Rubin Has Found Two More of the Milky Way's Dim Satellites
articles.description: The Vera Rubin Observatory has detected two more of the Milky Ways' dim, hard to see satellites. One is an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy, and one is a globular cluster. Each one is a missing piece of the puzzle in the Milky Way's merger history. By finding more of…
articles.summary: The Vera Rubin Observatory has discovered two additional faint satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way, expanding our understanding of galactic structure. This discovery highlights the power of modern observatories to detect previously hidden cosmic companions.

articles.title: Nanohertz Gravitational-Wave Constraints on Supermassive Binary Black Holes at Cosmic Dawn
articles.description: Author(s): Yiqin Chen, Shi-Yi Zhao, Xingjiang Zhu, N. D. Ramesh Bhat, Jacob Cardinal Tremblay, Małgorzata Curyło, Valentina Di Marco, George Hobbs, Wenhua Ling, Rami F. Mandow, Richard N. Manchester, Saurav Mishra, Daniel J. Reardon, Sparrow Roch, Christopher…
articles.summary: Researchers have used nanohertz gravitational waves to constrain the properties of supermassive binary black holes from the cosmic dawn era. This advancement opens new windows into understanding the earliest supermassive black holes in the universe.

articles.summary: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman discusses the Artemis III rocket inside the Vehicle Assembly Building in an energizing conversation about humanity's return to the Moon. This insight showcases NASA's commitment to advancing lunar exploration.

articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 to Cross Historic One Light-Day Milestone on Nov. 18
articles.description: Traveling one light-day took the space probe 49 years. it would take a human 612,015 years to walk that distance.
articles.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 will cross the historic one light-day distance milestone on November 18, after 49 years of interstellar travel. This achievement represents humanity's most distant active spacecraft and a triumph of engineering longevity.

articles.title: NASA to Welcome Expedition 74 Astronauts Home at Space Center Houston
articles.description: NASA will welcome home the Expedition 74 crew during a public event at Space Center Houston following their return from a long-duration mission aboard the International Space Station. NASA astronauts Jessica Meir, Jack Hathaway, and Chris Williams; ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot; and Roscosmos cosmonauts Sergey Kud‑Sverchkov and Sergei Mikaev will share mission […]
articles.summary: NASA welcomes home the Expedition 74 crew at Space Center Houston following their return from the International Space Station. The public event celebrates the astronauts' successful mission completion.

The crew recently exited their habitat on Saturday, Oct. 31, after 378 days of isolation in a facility at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Health […]
articles.summary: The CHAPEA Mission 2 crew documents their analog mission experiences, preparing humanity for future Mars exploration. This crew health and performance research advances our readiness for long-duration space missions.
